question: A researcher mentions in a chat that they prefer citations in APA format, but does not add this preference to the project knowledge base or project instructions. In a different chat within the same project, Claude does not apply APA formatting by default. Why does this occur?
options: A) Claude supports only one citation style per account for the entire lifetime of that account
B) The researcher's current plan does not support citation formatting inside project chats at all
C) Preferences mentioned only in a single chat are not shared across chats unless added to instructions
D) APA formatting is a feature that must be enabled separately in account-wide settings outside projects
correct_answers: C) Preferences mentioned only in a single chat are not shared across chats unless added to instructions
explanations: Incorrect. Citation style is not fixed for the lifetime of an account; it can be guided per project through instructions.
Incorrect. This behavior reflects how context persistence works, not a plan-based restriction on formatting styles.
Correct. Context shared in one chat is not shared across chats within a project unless it is captured in project instructions or added to the knowledge base.
Incorrect. There is no separate account-wide setting for citation style; persistence within a project is controlled through instructions or knowledge base content.
